sources.label: PD 1096 RIRR 2004, Rule IX (Sanitation) — Storm Drainage Requirements
sources.description: Requires storm drainage system as part of sanitary/site engineering. Must be separate from sanitary sewer system.

sources.label: PD 1067: Water Code of the Philippines, Articles 51-54 — Waterway Easements and Flood Control
sources.description: Article 51: 3m (urban), 20m (agricultural), 40m (forest) easement from river/creek banks. Articles 53-54: DPWH flood control areas; activities that obstruct flow are prohibited.

sources.label: DENR DAO 2016-08: Water Quality Guidelines and General Effluent Standards
sources.description: Stormwater discharge must not degrade receiving water body quality. Sediment basins may be required during construction.

sources.label: DPWH Design Guidelines — Design Storm Return Periods for Drainage
sources.description: Typical design storm: 10-year return period for commercial sites, 25-year for critical infrastructure, 5-year for residential.

sources.label: Rational Method (Q = CiA) — Standard Hydrologic Formula for Peak Runoff Estimation
sources.description: Standard formula for estimating peak stormwater runoff from small drainage areas (<20 hectares). Q = peak runoff, C = runoff coefficient, i = rainfall intensity, A = drainage area.

sources.label: Low-Impact Development (LID) Design Standards — Swale Specifications
sources.description: Swale side slopes max 3:1 (horizontal:vertical). Longitudinal slope 1-5%. Flow velocity should not exceed 1.0 m/s to prevent erosion in vegetated swales.
